newsitem.title: USA: N.H. lawmakers pass $5.6 bln biennial budget.
newsitem.headline: N.H. lawmakers pass $5.6 bln biennial budget.

text.p: After working into early Friday morning, New Hampshire lawmakers passed a $5.6 billion biennial budget, a statewide kindergarten program and a cigarette tax hike.
House-Senate budget conferees reconciled differing versions of the $5.6 billion plan after days of wrangling.
The compromise spending plan cuts Health and Human Service Department spending, funds a $20 million state employees contract and appropriates $16 million for a new kindergarten program.
The two-year spending plan also includes new revenue raisers such as taxing pay telephone calls and hiking the state's cigarette tax by 12 cents. The tax is currently 25 cents.
The kindergarten program is a victory for Gov. Jeanne Shaheen who promised during her campaign to expand kindergarten.
The Shaheen plan calls for a $40 million direct aid and classroom construction package.

But Shaheen did not get all that she wanted from the budget negotiations. The Senate defied her by insisting on a 12 cent hike of the cigarette tax rather than her plan to double it to 50 cents per pack.
